Chief RULING: CONFIRMED, filed P1, blast radius exactly as the scout bounded it - a BENCH SCORING defect, not an inference defect.

THE TRACE, which is what makes this fileable where the last one was not: AlignState.isExternal is !isSource, so External(Unranked) is counted by AlignmentRow.externalMass (matrix.scala:57,132). GraphHsmm gives an abstained or empty candidate set exclusively Unranked (hsmm.scala:546), and WorkedExampleSuite already PROVES such a row carries Unranked mass 1.0 with Intrusion 0.0. The single production consequence is Metrics.observe for open-world:external-over-source, where Association/Intrusion/Uninterpretable gold receives ind(row.externalMass > row.sourceMass) at metrics.scala:206-211. EXACT COUNTEREXAMPLE: an unrankable external-gold unit has externalMass 1 and sourceMass 0, SO IT SCORES 1.0 - a correct external call - DESPITE THE ALIGNER HAVING NO RANKING EVIDENCE AT ALL. That flows into MetricValue and renders under open-world metrics, so it can inflate benchmark evidence. It does not touch posterior inference.

WHY P1: it meets the estimand criterion exactly. Unrankable units are more common for sparse and disorganised recall, so the indicator is inflated precisely where alignment is hardest, in one direction - the flattering one. A bench that rewards us for being unable to rank a unit is measuring our failure as our success. And it feeds calibration evidence, which is the path to shipped defaults.

FIX DIRECTION, and ADR 0003 already decides it: hard classifications abstain, and the ADR explicitly separates Unranked from participant-attributed external content. So Unranked rows yield None with explicit missing support rather than a positive external decision. Adversarial regression required: show that abstention CANNOT IMPROVE external-rule accuracy - because the tempting wrong fix is to drop those rows, which would silently raise the score on the remaining ones, and that is the renormalization trap for the fifth time tonight.

WHAT I WANT NOTED ABOUT HOW THIS WENT. Thirty minutes ago I escalated an untraced consequence to P1 and had to retract it. This time I found a suspicious shape, TRACED IT PARTWAY, EXPLICITLY MARKED IT UNCONFIRMED, refused to file it on my own reading, and asked for the trace. The trace came back confirming the mechanism AND bounding it more narrowly than I would have - I would probably have said 'benchmark evidence is corrupted'; the correct statement is 'one open-world indicator is inflated for unrankable units, inference untouched'. The corrected process produced a better claim than my instinct would have, one cycle after the failure that taught it.
